beats.caption: A year after the battle, ashes remained at three places near the Alamo.
beats.camera: Pan between three separated reconstructed sites; exact coordinates are unknown.

beats.caption: Seguín gathers ashes. This quiet, solitary moment is a dramatization of the documented collection.
beats.camera: Move close enough to read his hands; return to a wider view before the next beat.

beats.caption: Ashes from the two smaller heaps were placed in a black-covered coffin and brought to the parish church.
beats.camera: Hold on the coffin; show flag, rifle and sword as separate readable details.

beats.caption: Seguín and his command led a public procession and paid military honors at the ash sites.
beats.camera: Wide procession composed from the existing soldier march clips; no combat fire or triumphant music.

beats.caption: Seguín later said he had placed remains in a grave inside San Fernando near the altar. His earlier account describes an outdoor interment.
beats.camera: An attributed memory vignette; visually distinguish it from the documented procession.

beats.caption: In 1936 a box of remains was found near the altar. Whether these were the Alamo defenders' remains remains disputed.
beats.camera: Dissolve between intact and opened floor; do not identify the contents visually.

beats.caption: The white marble memorial was made later; it was not Seguín's 1837 coffin.
beats.camera: End on a still shot and a source-accessible history note.
